title: Working together with an rn-craft React Native app

R1.reason: A single baseQuery's prepareHeaders sets Authorization with the Firebase ID token and X-App-Locale from i18n.resolvedLanguage.

R2.reason: toApiError keeps code, status (on server), requestId and Retry-After, and adds conflict and rateLimited kinds. Status is not kept on every variant, but this is minor.

R3.reason: applyApiErrors maps details[].field to setError, including dotted paths and a root.server fallback.

R4.reason: Page<T> matches { data, meta }, and an infiniteQuery uses meta.hasMore and nextCursor as the next page param.

R5.reason: Backend users.id is used for Adapty identify and analytics. The Firebase uid stays inside the auth service. Premium comes from me.entitlements on the backend, and isPremium is never sent.

R6.reason: Sign-out unlinks the device token before resetSession clears state. Re-registration on sign-in re-binds a token that belonged to another account, and the backend re-bind logic is shown.

R7.reason: One Idempotency-Key per user action, reused together with the body snapshot on retries. Writes are retried only when keyed.

R8.reason: States that the guide's changes are a proposed patch not merged into rn-craft, and flags where the answer goes beyond the guide. It does not claim rn-craft already supports these changes.

forbidden.item: Making rn-craft a dependency of the backend or the backend a dependency of the app.
forbidden.evidence: The answer generates schema.d.ts from the OpenAPI spec and says never to import backend packages.

forbidden.item: Trusting isPremium or userId from the client.
forbidden.evidence: The answer says never to send isPremium, reads entitlements from the backend, and says the user comes from the ID token, not the body.

forbidden.item: Generating a new idempotency key on each retry.
forbidden.evidence: The key and body are snapshotted in pending.current and reused while the outcome is unknown.

forbidden.item: Claiming rn-craft already supports these headers or error cases.
forbidden.evidence: The answer calls the guide's changes a proposed patch that is not merged, and lists them as changes to make.

grade.summary: The answer covers every rubric area correctly, is honest that the changes are proposed rather than already in rn-craft, and violates none of the forbidden decisions.
